title: Planning poker, story points and the fallacy of precision

videos.script: Five developers look at the same story. The senior one says: that's a three. {{anchor}} Everybody nods, and the estimate is now one person's estimate with extra steps. {{nods}} Planning poker fixes that with one rule. Everybody chooses a card in private, and everybody turns it over at once. {{reveal}} When one card says three and another says thirteen, the useful part of the meeting begins. Somebody knows something the others do not. {{disagree}} This lesson explains what a story point is, turns the Agenda team's last eight sprints into a forecast, and shows why the forecast is a range. {{forecast}} Then it names the four ways points get misused, and the habit behind most of them: a number stated more precisely than anybody knows it. {{precision}}
